handoff_instructions.purpose: Handoffs document the current state and scope of the project so a new LLM session can pick up exactly where the last one left off. They are the primary continuity mechanism for this project.
what_to_include: A summary of what was done, discussed, built, or decided in this session
What worked and what did not work
Current pipeline state — what scripts exist, what their status is, what the next steps are
A condensed recap of prior sessions so the new LLM has full project context without reading every previous handoff
Open questions or blockers that carry into the next session
what_not_to_include: Exhaustive code listings — reference file paths instead
Decisions that were reversed or abandoned mid-session — only document final state
Speculation about distant future work — stay close to what is actually next
format_rules: This handoff_instructions block must appear at the top of every future handoff
When a user says 'create a handoff for this session,' use this block as the template and fill in the session-specific fields
Prior session summaries should be condensed — one paragraph per session, not a full retelling
Be brief but complete. A new LLM should be able to start working immediately after reading this file

this_session.summary: Nolan ran the Mabrey Estates test and identified three extraction errors in Gemini's output: (1) missed 163.15 LF at the start of Mabrey Ave, (2) missed 189.98 LF at the end of Mabrey Ave, and (3) missed Swaboda Road entirely (163.81 LF). Gemini also guessed 50 ft ROW instead of reading the correct 88 ft (68' road arrow + 10' easement each side). Nolan met with Brian (the estimator) and brought back domain rules for manholes. We diagnosed root causes for all errors, then made a comprehensive set of improvements to m3_infer.py. Session ended with Nolan asking about 'Claude Fable 5' — confirmed it does not exist.

root_cause_analysis.missed_road_segments: Gemini was treating the Mabrey plat as a full civil plan set, expecting stationing and profiles. Finding none, it fell back to reading dimension callouts but missed endpoint segments (the short tangent runs where new road joins the existing street) and missed Swaboda Road entirely because there was no sheet title pointing to it.
root_cause_analysis.wrong_row_width: The old prompt said 'read from the typical section sheet.' Mabrey has no typical section, so Gemini guessed 50 ft from the easement text instead of computing 68' arrow + 10' + 10' = 88'.
root_cause_analysis.road_lf_null_in_chat_test: Gemini actively chose null over a rough calculation, reasoning that 'manual mathematical takeoff is highly prone to error.' The never-return-null directive was added to counter this.

change_1_plan_set_type_detection.description: Added STEP 1 / STEP 2 / STEP 3 structure to road_LF_hint extraction. STEP 1 classifies the plan set as Type A (full civil, per-road sheets with stationing) or Type B (plat/partial, roads in natural orientation identified by name text labels). STEP 2 finds all roads using title blocks for Type A and name text labels for Type B. STEP 3 adds SOURCE 6 for Type B: trace dimension callouts from start to end of each named road, including terminal segments at both endpoints.
change_1_plan_set_type_detection.key_text: CRITICAL: the segments at each road endpoint — where the new road joins an existing street — are the most commonly missed. Explicitly check both ends of every road before finalising its total.

change_2_never_return_null.description: Added hard 'NEVER RETURN NULL FOR ROAD_LF' directive explaining that null propagates as zero into all downstream items (sewer, water, curb, sidewalk, swales, dry utility trenching). A low-confidence estimate is always better than null.
change_2_never_return_null.confidence_schema: road_LF_confidence: high (single explicit stationing/callout), medium (summed from multiple visible callouts), low (partial segments, some inferred)

change_3_row_width_type_b.description: Added fallback for Type B plan sets: look for a dimension arrow spanning the road cross-section, then add labeled easements on each side. Provided explicit example: 68' arrow + 10' easements each side → 88'. Added 'Do NOT default to 50'' instruction.
change_3_row_width_type_b.confidence_schema: ROW_width_confidence: high (explicit typical section label), medium (arrow + easement math), low (inferred from easement text, no direct dimension)

change_4_json_schema.description: Added new fields to the Gemini JSON output schema: road_LF_confidence, ROW_width_confidence, proposed_manhole_count. road_LF_segments was already present.

change_5_proposed_manhole_count.description: New Gemini extraction field. Count ONLY explicitly labeled NEW/PROPOSED sewer manholes (MH symbols, callout bubbles, manhole schedule/table). Return null if not explicitly labeled — do not estimate.
change_5_proposed_manhole_count.rationale: When plans do label manholes, Gemini's count is more reliable than the inference rules.

change_6_sidecar_output.description: Updated the Gemini extraction sidecar markdown to include road_LF_confidence, ROW_width_confidence, and proposed_manhole_count fields.

change_7_manhole_rules.description: Rewrote the SEWER MANHOLES inference rule in the Claude prompt with Brian's domain knowledge. Old rule was a single formula round(sewer_main_LF / 250). New rule has: PRIORITY path (use proposed_manhole_count from Gemini if not null, flag as [FROM PLANS]); RULE A intersection-based placement (cul_de_sac=1, straight_through=2, arc_loop=2, multi_branch=3-4); RULE B spacing (ceil(sewer_main_LF / 350)); RECONCILE by walking sewer main and placing manholes at intersections OR when cumulative distance > 350 LF, whichever first (minimum 250 LF spacing); ADDITIONAL TRIGGERS (+1 each for bend >30°, pipe diameter transition, terminal dead-end branch). Note: sewer follows gravity; flag [GRAVITY DIRECTION ASSUMED] if terrain not readable.
change_7_manhole_rules.source: Brian's verbal domain rules, captured in this session

change_8_curb_and_sidewalk.description: Added EXISTING ROAD CAVEAT to curb rule: if Terra is doing frontage improvements on an existing road, apply curb only to side(s) Terra is fronting. One-side: road_LF × 1.0, flag [ONE-SIDE FRONTAGE]. Added new item 7 SIDEWALK SF: almost always 5 ft wide; sidewalk_SF = road_LF × 5 (one side, default) or road_LF × 10 (both sides); same existing-road caveat applies; price from unit_price_distributions for '4" SIDEWALKS' or '6" SIDEWALKS', default to 4". Irrigation sleeves renumbered to item 8.

claude_fable_5_question.question: Nolan asked whether swapping the .env Gemini model variable to 'Claude Fable 5' would test Claude vision capabilities.
claude_fable_5_question.answer: 'Claude Fable 5' does not exist. Anthropic's model families are Opus, Sonnet, and Haiku — there is no Fable line. Current models: claude-opus-4-8, claude-sonnet-4-6, claude-haiku-4-5. Additionally, swapping the env variable would not work: gemini_extract() calls the Google Generative AI SDK; claude_infer() calls the Anthropic SDK. These are different APIs and different clients. Testing Claude for vision extraction would require rewriting gemini_extract() to use the Anthropic API with base64 image content blocks.

operational_constraints.never_run_python_scripts_directly: Tell the user the command and wait for them to paste output. Never execute python scripts.

operational_constraints.version_alignment: PDF/DWG/qty-sheet/proposal per job may be different revisions. Nolan verifies manually — do not automate cross-document version matching.
